speaker: Sheldon
text: I know. Although I've always hated how my right frontal lobe looks in pictures.

speaker: Dr. Beverly Hofstadter
text: Your scan data will be very helpful to my research. You have a remarkable brain. Common complaint among men. Nothing's ever big enough. Except when they get a tumor, then you never hear the end of it.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I'd love to see a scan of your brain sometime.

speaker: Dr. Beverly Hofstadter
text: Oh, I'll send you a link, but its physiology is fairly unimpressive.

speaker: Dr. Beverly Hofstadter
text: Your unwillingness to accept empirical evidence suggests an attempt at flattery.

speaker: Sheldon
text: My apologies. I've been living with your son too long, gotten into some bad habits.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Can I make you a cup of tea?

speaker: Dr. Beverly Hofstadter
text: I doubt it, but if anyone has a chance, it's probably you.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I feel very comfortable around you.

speaker: Dr. Beverly Hofstadter
text: I feel very comfortable around you, too.

speaker: Sheldon
text: It's surprising, because I generally don't feel comfortable around anyone.

speaker: Sheldon
text: What are the odds that two individuals as unique as ourselves would be connected by someone as comparatively workaday as your son?

speaker: Dr. Beverly Hofstadter
text: Is that a rhetorical point, or would you like to do the math?

speaker: Sheldon
text: I'd like to do the math.
